page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-4 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It is equipped with 15.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1916.0 and a single-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 14.04 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are relatively weak. The multi-core Geekbench score is 4292.0, and the stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is 3746.88. Memory bandwidth for uncached large blocks is limited to 29.4 GB/sec for read operations and 18.6 GB/sec for write operations. Static web serving throughput is moderate at 8.14 GB/sec, while Redis SET operations reach 5.84 million operations per second.

The c4-standard-4 offers a balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio suitable for general-purpose workloads. Its qualitative cost efficiency is characterized by dedicated Intel Xeon compute resources without the added expense of bundled local storage or GPU hardware. The primary tradeoff is the contrast between its strong single-core capabilities and its weaker multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth. It is best suited for workloads that prioritize single-threaded execution, such as text processing, basic web serving, and lightweight single-threaded applications, rather than memory-intensive databases or highly parallelized compilation tasks.
